panels.title: E06 · When will this batch or project get usable GPUs?
panels.description: Missing input, release R3: no number is shown. Contract: config/panel-contracts/ttv-capacity.yaml (panel 1).

options.content:
**Release R3 · missing input.** This card shows no number until the inputs below exist.

**What it will show.** Per procurement batch or project: the committed date against forecast ranges for GPU-ready and user-accessible, observed progress, blocking prerequisites and delivery risk. Each forecast states its as-of time, method, input coverage and uncertainty and is backtested against a simple baseline; no date comes from a single fleet-wide average.

**Missing inputs**

| Input | Where it would come from |
| --- | --- |
| Procurement batches and their servers (vendor + serial) | Versioned CSV/YAML import or small API from procurement records |
| Project capacity requests and approved commitment dates | Same import, each with ID, owner, effective dates, review and expiry |
| Enough completed episodes per comparable segment to forecast | Ledger milestones, accumulating since the first scan |
| Calendars or freeze windows, where they matter | Configuration |

**Onboarding step.** Import batches and commitments, join their servers to assets by vendor and normalised serial, and enable the forecast once its backtest has enough history.

**Answer today (R1).** [Delivery](/d/ttv-delivery) shows observed p50/p90 time to GPU-ready and to first genuine request (≥ where lower-bounded); [Asset](/d/ttv-asset) shows one server's milestones.

panels.title: E08 · Do we need to buy more—or can we use what we own?
panels.description: Missing input, release R3: no number is shown. Contract: config/panel-contracts/ttv-capacity.yaml (panel 2).

options.content:
**Release R3 · missing input.** This card shows no number until the inputs below exist.

**What it will show.** Compatible capacity available now, recoverable after an intervention, reserved, incoming and required by validated demand, with a dated shortfall scenario. A fit check (GPU model and memory, node shape and interconnect, whole-node or gang scheduling, locality, isolation, SLOs) decides what is compatible; incoming servers never count as available today.

**Missing inputs**

| Input | Where it would come from |
| --- | --- |
| Validated demand: capacity requests, scheduler queues, forecasts (deduplicated) | Versioned import or API; pending scheduler queues read from the clusters (read-only) |
| Reservations and approved headroom | Reservation register (see E17) |
| Incoming supply: orders and expected receipt dates | Procurement import (see E06) |
| Workload fit profiles | Fit-check policy per workload class, in configuration |
| Capacity recoverable per action | Action ledger (E05, Actions) |

**Onboarding step.** Import demand, reservations and orders and configure fit-check profiles; the page then splits owned capacity into these buckets without counting a GPU twice.

**Answer today (R1).** [Queues](/d/ttv-queues) shows GPUs idle now by stage owner and reason, i.e. capacity we own but do not use; [GPU use](/d/ttv-gpu-use) shows allocation and activity.

panels.title: E09 · How much more demand can we serve safely?
panels.description: Missing input, release R3: no number is shown. Contract: config/panel-contracts/ttv-capacity.yaml (panel 3).

options.content:
**Release R3 · missing input.** This card shows no number until the inputs below exist.

**What it will show.** Sustainable goodput and headroom for a defined model, context/output mix and SLO, against current, queued and planned demand, with the binding constraint and forecast coverage. Without a calibrated benchmark it says *unsupported estimate* instead of turning GPU utilisation into users.

**Missing inputs**

| Input | Where it would come from |
| --- | --- |
| Workload benchmarks: model, precision, context/output mix, versions, SLO limits | Benchmark import from approved runs (no load test is launched for this page) |
| Service SLOs (latency, success) per service | Configuration, approved by the service owner |
| Traffic per logical deployment (one counter of record) | Service graph and serving metrics through Thanos (R2, see Service) |
| Demand history and growth plans | Ledger history and the demand import (see E08) |

**Onboarding step.** After the R2 service graph, import benchmark profiles with their conditions and set SLOs per service; headroom then appears per model with its assumptions.

**Answer today (R1).** [GPU use](/d/ttv-gpu-use) shows which GPUs carry genuine traffic and which are allocated but idle.

panels.title: E14 · What capacity and services are at risk?
panels.description: Missing input, release R3: no number is shown. Contract: config/panel-contracts/ttv-capacity.yaml (panel 4).

options.content:
**Release R3 · missing input.** This card shows no number until the inputs below exist.

**What it will show.** Verified failure-domain concentrations (site, rack, power feed, network, cluster), critical dependencies, the capacity a specified outage would remove, and validated failover headroom where it exists. A logical dependency is never shown as a proven failover result, and unknown dependencies are marked.

**Missing inputs**

| Input | Where it would come from |
| --- | --- |
| Verified topology: rack, PDU or power feed and network domain per server | CMDB/NetBox or a versioned topology import |
| Service importance and criticality | Service importance import, owner-approved |
| Service-to-server dependency graph | Service graph from the clusters, read-only (R2) |
| Approved failover policy and failover-test evidence | Engineering input |

**Onboarding step.** Import topology and service importance; the page then groups capacity by failure domain and keeps unknown dependencies visible.

**Answer today (R1).** [Queues](/d/ttv-queues): the reason breakdown counts GPUs held by maintenance, critical hardware health or unreachable BMCs; [Evidence](/d/ttv-evidence) shows source health and coverage.

panels.title: E17 · Is reserved capacity still justified?
panels.description: Missing input, release R3: no number is shown. Contract: config/panel-contracts/ttv-capacity.yaml (panel 5).

options.content:
**Release R3 · missing input.** This card shows no number until the inputs below exist.

**What it will show.** Each reservation or commitment with its owner, purpose, expiry, usage evidence, priority and renewal status, separating approved reliability headroom from abandoned allocations.

**Missing inputs**

| Input | Where it would come from |
| --- | --- |
| Reservation register: owner, purpose, servers or GPUs, start, expiry, renewal, approved-headroom flag | Versioned import or small API |
| Intentional exclusions (open input I5) | Policy configuration; the list is empty today |
| Project priority | Approved priority list (shared with E05) |
| Usage evidence per reserved GPU | Already in the ledger: the category of every GPU |

**Onboarding step.** Import reservations and join them to assets by vendor and serial or by node; the page then compares each reservation with what its GPUs actually did.

**Answer today (R1).** [Queues](/d/ttv-queues) shows NOT_CHARGED GPUs (approved exclusions) and their reasons; [GPU use](/d/ttv-gpu-use) shows whether held GPUs do work.
